messages:
maya: noticed a bunch of model-sync jobs stuck in 'receiving' on node-pool-gpu-3, grpc streams hang mid-chunk. Started ~09:10 UTC, p99 token stream latency spikes to 30s. :eyes:
chris: any packet loss metrics from that time? which nodes?
maya: pod A -> pod B (different AZ within region), node ip 10.4.7.12 -> 10.4.18.9. kube-proxy NAT seemed fine, flows established but grpc stream stalls. I grabbed tcpdump on both ends, attached excerpt: ```12:03:21.123456 IP 10.4.7.12.45678 > 10.4.18.9.443: Flags [.], seq 1:1401, ack 1, win 29200, length 1400``` then later: ```12:03:21.123789 IP (frag) 10.4.7.12 > 10.4.18.9: ICMP pmtu 1500 bytes needed``` so looks like fragmentation / PMTU event.
aj: that ICMP suggests overlay/encap increased packet size (vxlan/geneve). Do we have different MTU at node NIC vs host-OS vs kube-cni overlay? run `ip link` + `ip route get` maybe. Also check `ethtool -k` for GSO/TSO/GRO.
maya: ran `ip link` on both nodes: `eth0 mtu 9000` but `vxlan0 mtu 1450` on nodeB. CNI is calico+vxlan. ethtool -k shows tso/gso/gro on.
olivia: hm we saw something similar last quarter in ap-northeast: VXLAN outer header plus ipsec introduced ~50 bytes and one side had sidenode MTU clamped by cloud-vpc. Packets above path MTU got blackholed until tcp_mtu_probing synced.
sam: quick mitigation: disable segmentation offloads on the host NIC for affected nodes (DaemonSet) and reduce pod MTU to 1400 in CNI. Did you try `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off`?
maya: tried `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` on node-pool-gpu-3, grpc streams recovered for active sessions (latencies back to normal), new sessions ok. We saw model-shard transfers complete. :thumbsup:
chris: nice. We need to be careful — turning off offloads increases CPU on pNICs (could affect GPU node throughput). Any CPU bump?
maya: CPU on node jumped ~6% per NIC CPU core based on `sar` short window; acceptable for now but not ideal under sustained load.
aj: propose two-track fix: 1) roll CNI MTU change (reduce overlay MTU to account for encap) and 2) conservative daemonset to disable TSO/GSO/GRO only on nodes that hit the PMTU mismatch detection (auto remediation). Also enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` clusterwide to avoid blackholes during gradual change.
olivia: +1. Add a verification step: `sudo tcpdump -nn -s0 -w - 'ip[6:2] & 0x3fff != 0'` to detect fragments and `ip -s link` to check dropped frames. Tag me for rollout.
sam: I'll draft the daemonset (affects all nodepools) and a canary for 10% of GPU nodes in us-west1. We should also push a firmware check for mellanox nic drivers — we saw older firmwares misreport header size.
infra-bot: alert: node-pool-gpu-3 had flow-local metric spike at 2026-09-18T09:11:04Z - grpc-stream-hang detected. Auto-notify created INCIDENT-2026-348.
maya: created a short runbook note and linked incident. Runbook excerpt: "symptoms: grpc streaming stalls on pod-to-pod across nodes; quick checks: ip link, ethtool -k, tcpdump for ICMP pmtu, disable offloads to confirm. Mitigation: disable TSO/GSO/GRO, reduce overlay MTU, enable tcp_mtu_probing. Long term: align CNI overlay MTU with VPC path MTU and validate NIC firmware."
chris: next actions: sam to PR daemonset + docs; aj to coordinate CNI config change and schedule 1-hour window for canary; olivia to run firmware audit for RDMA NICs; maya to monitor incident and mark resolved when no new stalls for 2 hours.
maya: thanks all — monitoring now, will update thread when stable. :wave:
